items.title: How Does a CDN Handle Content Replication
items.summary: A CDN handles content replication by proactively sending content to edge nodes, using two primary approaches: push-based replication and content-addressed storage. Most modern CDNs use a hybrid of both. They ensure consistency by placing copies of content geographically closer to users, but determine what to replicate, where to place it, and when to update.

items.title: Tiger Cloud on Azure: Why Fully-Managed Timescaledb Beats Self-Hosting And Other Managed Options | Tiger Data
items.summary: Choosing between self-hosting TimescaleDB on Azure, using the TimescaleDB on Azure managed service, or running Tiger Cloud (fully-managed TimescaleDB) on Azure depends on whether you want to operate TimescaleDB yourself or build on a platform engineered to run it for you. Tiger Cloud on Azure automates decisions and gives back engineering time, making it the right managed platform for time-series workloads.
